title: Principality of Nitra
capsule: The Principality of Nitra was a West Slavic polity that emerged in the early 9th century around the fortified site of Nitra in present-day southwestern Slovakia, considered by historians the first demonstrable Slavic state north of the middle Danube. Its ruler Pribina held court there until approximately 833, when Mojmir I of Moravia expelled him, absorbing Nitra into what became Great Moravia. Pribina subsequently fled to East Francia, where he was baptized under King Louis the German, and later received the Pannonian principality of Balaton as a Frankish vassal. The Nitrian territory continued as a duchy within Great Moravia and later within the Kingdom of Hungary, administered by members of the Árpád dynasty, preserving a distinct regional identity that would become a touchstone of Slovak national historiography.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's existence is inferred from limited Frankish and later medieval sources; its precise territorial extent is a matter of scholarly debate rather than cartographic record.
